open_points.subject: R0-12 and A14 document binary failure mapping
open_points.text: R0-12 says "a refused document read answers that way also when its stored content is missing, oversize or unlisted", making those failures indistinguishable from an unknown, cross-project or hidden read; A14 says "A missing source object is an explicit unavailable/not-found failure" and separately says oversize and unlisted content are rejected.
open_points.question: Must every missing, oversize or unlisted expense-document failure use exactly the concealed unknown/hidden response, or may any of them be exposed as a distinct unavailable or content-policy failure under A14?
options: Conceal all three exactly like an unknown, cross-project or hidden document
Expose missing as storage unavailable while concealing or separately rejecting the other failures
Use A14's unavailable/not-found choice independently for each failure
open_points.default_guess: Apply the newer R0-12 rule and conceal all three exactly like an unknown or unauthorized document read.

witness.initial: A viewer has an active session and grant, and an expense document is client-visible, but its file_ref names a missing object.
events: The viewer requests the document by document_id.
The domain authorization and visibility checks pass, then binary storage reports the object missing.
outcomes: The response is identical to the response for an unknown or hidden document, as R0-12 requires.
The response is a distinct storage-unavailable failure, which A14's "unavailable/not-found" wording permits.
witness.observer: The authenticated viewer can distinguish whether the authorized document record exists and its storage is broken.

open_points.subject: R0-12 and A14 photo binary failure mapping
open_points.text: R0-12 says "a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error"; A14 says a missing source object is an "unavailable/not-found failure", while oversize and unlisted content are only described as rejected.
open_points.question: Which exact photo failures count as "stored content cannot be delivered", and must missing, oversize, unlisted media, unreadable storage and invalid file references all become the same storage-unavailable error rather than not-found or a distinct size/media/storage error?
options: Every post-authorization storage or content-delivery failure becomes one storage-unavailable error
Only missing storage becomes storage-unavailable; oversize and unlisted media keep distinct rejection kinds
Only the three named conditions—missing, oversize and unlisted—become storage-unavailable; other storage failures retain separate errors
open_points.default_guess: Map missing, oversize, unlisted and ordinary storage-read failures after successful photo authorization to one storage-unavailable error; keep malformed or unsafe references as separate internal integrity failures.

witness.initial: A staff member is authorized to read a visible progress photo, but the stored bytes exceed binary_max_read_bytes.
events: The staff member requests the photo by photo_id.
Authorization succeeds and storage detects that the content is oversize.
outcomes: The caller receives the explicit storage-unavailable error because the photo cannot be delivered.
The caller receives a distinct size-limit rejection because A14 describes oversize content separately and never assigns it the storage-unavailable error.
witness.observer: The authenticated staff caller sees a different error classification and later HTTP mapping.
